raw_requirements: Students, professors, and academic administrators are specialized roles of a university user. An authenticated identity and role are preconditions for protected operations.
A university user shall search published course offerings and inspect their course, section, instructor, meeting schedule, capacity, and remaining-seat information.
A student shall register for a selected course offering during its registration period and receive the result.
A student shall atomically swap a current registration for another course offering and receive the result.

Before either a registration or a swap is accepted, the system shall perform the same mandatory enrollment-eligibility validation, including registration-period, duplicate-enrollment, capacity, and timetable-conflict checks.
A student shall view current registrations and the resulting class schedule.
A student shall drop a selected registration during the allowed period and receive the result.

While viewing the current class schedule, a student may optionally export it in a downloadable format using the information already presented by that view. Viewing the schedule remains complete without an export.
When registration is rejected only because an offering is full and its waitlist is enabled, the student may join the waitlist. The rejected registration remains a complete result without joining.
A student shall view and cancel their own waitlist entries.
A professor shall review assigned course offerings and their current student rosters.
An academic administrator shall create and update academic terms and their registration periods.
An academic administrator shall create, update, publish, or cancel course offerings and assign their instructor, meeting schedule, and enrollment capacity.
The system shall authorize each protected operation according to the authenticated university-user role.
Course, offering, term, university-user, registration, and waitlist information shall survive application and server restarts.
Concurrent registration, swap, drop, and waitlist operations shall preserve enrollment capacity, registration uniqueness, and waitlist ordering.
resource_constraints_text: The university will pilot the service in the AWS Seoul Region (ap-northeast-2), and the monthly cloud budget must not exceed 500 USD. The fixed research scope is Docker on Linux virtual machines with Terraform and temporary HTTP endpoints. HTTPS, TLS certificates, and domain management are outside this pilot. The pilot may not use a managed database service, Kubernetes, or serverless compute and must use synthetic data instead of real personal data. Recovery from a data-storage server failure is outside this pilot.

actors.name: University User
actors.description: Any authenticated person who belongs to the university (student, professor, or academic‑administrator). The role and identity are required before any protected operation can be performed.

actors.name: Student
actors.description: A university user whose primary goal is to manage personal enrollment – searching offerings, registering, swapping, dropping, viewing schedules, and handling wait‑list entries.

actors.name: Professor
actors.description: A university user whose goal is to review the course offerings assigned to them and see the current rosters of enrolled students.

actors.name: Academic Administrator
actors.description: A university user responsible for configuring the academic calendar (terms and registration periods) and for creating, publishing, updating, or canceling course offerings, including instructor assignment and capacity settings.

use_cases.name: Search Course Offerings
use_cases.goal: Search published course offerings and inspect their details.

use_cases.name: Register for Course Offering
use_cases.goal: Register for a selected course offering during its registration period and receive the result.

use_cases.name: Swap Course Registration
use_cases.goal: Atomically swap a current registration for another course offering and receive the result.

use_cases.name: View Current Registrations and Schedule
use_cases.goal: View current registrations and the resulting class schedule.

use_cases.name: Drop Course Registration
use_cases.goal: Drop a selected registration during the allowed period and receive the result.

use_cases.name: Export Class Schedule
use_cases.goal: Export the currently viewed class schedule in a downloadable format.

use_cases.name: Join Waitlist for Full Course
use_cases.goal: Join the waitlist for a course offering when registration is rejected because the offering is full and waitlist is enabled.

use_cases.name: Cancel Waitlist Entry
use_cases.goal: Cancel a previously created waitlist entry.

use_cases.name: Review Assigned Course Offerings and Rosters
use_cases.goal: Review assigned course offerings and their current student rosters.

use_cases.name: Manage Academic Term
use_cases.goal: Create and update academic terms and their registration periods.

use_cases.name: Manage Course Offering
use_cases.goal: Create, update, publish, or cancel course offerings and assign instructor, meeting schedule, and enrollment capacity.
